text:
2.
In one simple linear regression model, we have sample size \(n=10\), \(\bar{x}=1.03\), \(\bar{y}=2.51\),
\[
\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i^{2}=20.37,\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^{n} y_i^{2}=116.56,\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i y_i=46.85.
\]
a) Find the values of the least squares estimators: \(\hat{\beta}_0\) and \(\hat{\beta}_1\).
b) Calculate \(\mathrm{SST}\), \(\mathrm{SSR}\), and \(\mathrm{SSE}\).
c) Calculate the sample estimate of the variance \(\sigma^{2}\) for the regression model.
d) What is the value of \(R^{2}\) here?
Hint. The following formulae may be useful (can be used without proof):
\[
\sum (x_i-\bar{x})^2
=
\sum x_i^2-n\bar{x}^{\,2},
\]
\[
\sum (x_i-\bar{x})(y_i-\bar{y})
=
\sum x_i y_i-n\bar{x}\,\bar{y}.
\]

title: STAT200C Assignment 1
text:
3.
Consider the simple linear regression model
\[
y_i=\beta_0+\beta_1x_i+\varepsilon_i,\qquad i=1,\ldots,n,
\]
where we assume:

\(\mathbb{E}(\varepsilon_i)=0,\ \forall i\);
\(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i)=\sigma^2,\ \forall i\);
\(\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_i,\varepsilon_j)=0,\ \forall i,j\text{ with }i\neq j\).

For the following questions, prove or verify the results. You can choose either one of the two ways:

Prove: You can prove them mathematically.
Verify: You can verify them using a data set (real or simulated) in R. Be sure to show your code and the results.


a)
For the least squares estimators \(\hat{\beta}_0\) and \(\hat{\beta}_1\), the following hold.
\[
\text{i.}\quad
\hat{\beta}_1
=
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i-\bar{y})(x_i-\bar{x})}
{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_i-\bar{x})^2},
\]
\[
\text{ii.}\quad
\hat{\beta}_1
=
\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}y_i\,(x_i-\bar{x})}
{\sum_{i=1}^{n}(x_i-\bar{x})^2}.
\]



b)
Let the residuals be
\[
e_i=y_i-\hat{\beta}_0-\hat{\beta}_1x_i.
\]
The following holds:
\[
0
=
\sum_{i=1}^{n}x_i e_i
=
\sum_{i=1}^{n}e_i
=
\sum_{i=1}^{n}\hat{y}_i e_i.
\]
